passages.note: Golden Together report Hilton signed as founder (body's lead author is named as Edward Ring, so attribution is borderline); 'restructuring or eliminating rent control' shows the anti-rent-control side but does not choose between rungs 3, 4 and 5, and it predates the 2026 campaign.
Starter-home plan on the campaign site addresses building supply and fees, not rent rules or how many units they cover.
VMT mitigation-fee plan concerns construction costs, not rent regulation.
Debate housing answer covers regulations, lawsuits and single-family building, and says nothing about rent control or tenant protections.

rows.reasoning: The only on-question passage, the 2024 Golden Together report, says "Restructuring or eliminating rent control and subsidized affordable housing ... will free up investment". That puts it on the side against rent control. But "restructuring or eliminating" does not choose between "Maintain current tenant protections while allowing market rents for new construction", "Limit rent regulations to subsidized units" and "Oppose rent control entirely". It also predates the campaign. His 2026 campaign housing material does not address rent rules.
needs_source: Hilton's own 2026-campaign words on rent control or the Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482), e.g. a candidate questionnaire or a debate answer on rent regulation

quotes.text: Restructuring or eliminating rent control and subsidized affordable housing, in particular, the special incentives for high density housing, will free up investment to build housing on the scale we need.
